Chapter 9: Passing On Faith to the Next Generation.
You know, there’s a quiet hope that lives inside every parent, grandparent, or mentor. It’s that deep desire—the kind that keeps you up at night sometimes—that the next generation will truly know and love God.
But here’s the thing: passing on faith isn’t about giving grand speeches or having all the answers. It’s really about living out what matters most, day after day, in the ordinary moments.
Imagine a mom tucking her child into bed at night. She pauses for just a moment so they can pray together before the lights go out. The words aren’t fancy—they don’t have to be—but the habit is powerful. Over time, these little moments become the foundation for how a child experiences God’s love and faithfulness.
What a lot of people don’t realize is just how much kids pick up by watching, not just listening. There’s this one woman who was constantly worried she wasn’t doing enough to teach her kids about faith. But then, it hit her: her actions were speaking even louder than her words ever could. When her children saw her reading her Bible, helping others, and turning to prayer whenever things got tough, they learned what trusting God really looked like.
Passing on faith happens in the everyday stuff—sharing stories from Scripture, talking about God’s goodness, and inviting kids to pray about their worries and dreams. It’s about making space for questions, and meeting doubts with patience instead of judgment.
Of course, there are seasons when it feels like nothing’s getting through. Maybe your child pushes back or even drifts away for a while. In those moments, you realize something important: faith is ultimately a work of God’s Spirit. Parents and mentors can plant seeds, but only God can make them grow. And that’s actually comforting—it means your role is to be faithful, not perfect.
As the years go by, you start to notice just how much a life of integrity really matters. Kids remember how their parents treated people, how they handled disappointments, and how they celebrated blessings. Those memories? They shape how the next generation sees faith for themselves.
